what_happens: An agency drafts a rule it has authority to issue; "rule making" covers "formulating, amending, or repealing a rule"
source_words: "rule making" means agency process for formulating, amending, or repealing a rule

step: White House review of a significant draft
who_acts: Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OMB)
what_happens: For a significant rule, the agency sends its draft and analysis for review before publishing
time_limit: 90 calendar days (10 working days for preliminary actions)
legal_basis: Executive Order 12866, section 6(b)(2), as amended; Executive Order 14215, section 3
source_words: OIRA shall waive review or notify the agency in writing of the results of its review "within 90 calendar days after the date of submission"; Executive Order 14215 extends the order to independent regulatory agencies, outside the Federal Reserve’s monetary policy

what_happens: The agency publishes a notice of proposed rule making in the Federal Register
source_words: "General notice of proposed rule making shall be published in the Federal Register"

what_happens: Any interested person may send written data, views or arguments; the agency considers them
time_limit: Not set by statute; Executive Order 12866 asks for "not less than 60 days" in most cases
source_words: "the agency shall give interested persons an opportunity to participate in the rule making through submission of written data, views, or arguments"

what_happens: The agency publishes the final rule with a statement of its basis and purpose
time_limit: At least 30 days before it takes effect, with exceptions
source_words: published "not less than 30 days before its effective date"

what_happens: Before a rule takes effect, the agency reports it to both houses of Congress and the Comptroller General
time_limit: Before the rule takes effect; a major rule waits at least 60 days
source_words: a major rule takes effect no sooner than "60 days after" Congress receives the report or the rule is published

what_happens: A joint resolution of disapproval passes both chambers and is signed, or a veto is overridden; the rule has no effect and a substantially similar rule needs a new law
time_limit: Introduced within 60 days of the report; the Senate fast track lasts 60 session days
source_words: "A rule shall not take effect (or continue), if the Congress enacts a joint resolution of disapproval"

what_happens: A person harmed by a final rule can sue; a court sets aside a rule that is arbitrary, capricious or not in accordance with law, among other grounds
source_words: "final agency action for which there is no other adequate remedy in a court" is "subject to judicial review"

what_happens: Interpretive rules and policy statements skip notice and comment unless a statute requires them
source_words: notice and comment do not apply "to interpretative rules, general statements of policy, or rules of agency organization, procedure, or practice"

what_happens: Any interested person may petition the agency to issue, amend or repeal a rule
source_words: "Each agency shall give an interested person the right to petition for the issuance, amendment, or repeal of a rule"
